rule: split keyId by colon into label value pairs
notes: empty keyId is invalid and token count must be even

rule: every segment must use the form label:value
notes: this removes ambiguity from bare labels

rule: underscore means intrinsic and tilde means contextual self reference
notes: all other values are opaque identifiers

rule: each label:value pair is one atomic segment
notes: semantic interpretation comes from labels and position instead of a duplicated segment kind field

rule: the parser must validate by traversing a schema from an allowed root label through child labels until the first configured anchor label is reached and then through descendant child labels
notes: path ordering and child rules are declarative rather than hardcoded

rule: each schema node defines allowed value types child labels and whether the node is terminal
notes: this keeps grammar logic in data instead of parser branches

rule: the schema may be a DAG because different parents may reference the same child label
notes: cycles must still be rejected during schema validation

rule: a label is repeatable only when it appears in its own childLabels set
notes: no separate repeatability flag is required

rule: rootLabels define which labels may start a validated key before any anchor is reached
notes: this validates scope under the same graph model as the anchored path

rule: maximum depth is defined in schema config in segment units
notes: the parser counts label:value pairs rather than raw colon-delimited tokens

rule: identifier values must satisfy schema-level minimum length maximum length and identifier alphabet policy
notes: this applies only to id values and not to labels or reserved values underscore or tilde

rule: identifier character validation should use direct code-unit checks against the configured idAlphabet preset and explicit extra characters
notes: this avoids regex-based policy evaluation and supports common forms such as lowercase hexadecimal UUID values

rule: schema labels are validated independently from id values
notes: labels are schema tokens and should use a tighter parser-defined rule than the configurable identifier alphabet

rule: terminal nodes are determined by schema and must declare an empty childLabels array and reject children
notes: no hardcoded terminal label checks are required in parser code

rule: canonical serialization always emits explicit label:value pairs
notes: the serializer does not need shape-specific exceptions
